bluf: SALT.agency is a Horsforth, Leeds enterprise SEO consultancy, with offices in London, Leeds and Boston, that sells technical SEO and AI search visibility to global brands and keeps its scope deliberately narrow. The record shows it building an AI search research and tooling line, an Entity Strength Index and a study of 107,352 sites cited in Google AI Mode, while its 2026 case studies still prove organic traffic and revenue. Its book holds 13 clients, 13 observed and 0 names only. A rival should know it sells AI visibility with no llms.txt and no audited AI visibility product in the record.
doing:
SALT.agency sells search to large brands and little else. Its positioning line, a specialist enterprise SEO and AI visibility consultancy for global brands, anchored in deep technical SEO and deliberately narrow in scope, means: grow the organic channel of big sites, and now their presence in AI answers, without selling media, builds or social. The headline claim is an award: its Swaledale campaign won Best Large SEO Campaign at the UK Agency Awards. The year is not shown; the case study is dated 2023-09-18.

The sold mix leads with SEO and AI Search / GEO, both scored 3. The SEO evidence is enterprise and technical cases for JetBrains, GitLab, Cloudflare and Jewson; the AI evidence is an AI search page, the ESI metric and 31 AI search URLs including AI Mode research. Content & Digital PR scores 2 on an SEO Content Services line with SaaS content writing, content hub and technical content audit pages. AI Automation, B2B & ABM, Data & Measurement and Local score 1 without notes; Paid Search, Paid Social and Web & Product score 0. The proprietary list names the Entity Strength Index, a Cloudflare methodology for seeing when ChatGPT uses content, and free tools: GSC BigQuery SQL Hero, Server Log File Googlebot Filter, Bulk Redirect Generator and Social Profile Checker. The record lists no partner.

Its AI posture ranks AI visibility as equal to SEO: AI search optimisation, agentic readiness audits, the ESI and published research on ChatGPT and AI Mode citations. The one move on record, the award, is undated. The case library runs from The Spectator (2019-08-29) through Cloudflare (2023-04-28), Swaledale (2023-09-18) and TCGplayer (2024-01-18) to JetBrains (2026-01-30), a yacht charter platform (2026-03-17), Qodana (2026-03-31) and Jewson (2026-05-20). The record lists no pricing signal, headcount, founding year, news or open roles, conspicuous beside 40 case studies, and no audited AI visibility product, conspicuous for a firm selling AI visibility.
clients:
The client type is enterprise, across transport and logistics, manufacturing, finance and fintech, travel, franchise, automotive, healthcare, energy, retail and ecommerce, fashion, and cloud and SaaS, sold from Horsforth, Leeds with offices in London, Leeds and Boston. The needs read holds 13 clients, 13 observed and 0 names only, and organic demand dominates: 12 clients carry it, a 0.661 share of the mix.

Cloudflare came for organic demand: US organic traffic rose from 22.4K to 235.9K visits a month over three years, a 318% rise (2023-04-28). JetBrains came for non branded organic traffic (40% growth, 2026-01-30), and Qodana, listed both alone and as Qodana (JetBrains) on one case study URL, for position one rankings (up 1650% through a content and SEO strategy, 2026-03-31). Jewson came for organic demand and commerce (ecommerce revenue from organic search up 7% despite declining demand, 2026-05-20). GitLab, Coralogix and The Pen Company came for organic demand on slug evidence; University of Leeds for web build (technical excellence during a UX and UI redesign); Bikmo and The Spectator for migrations, the latter with 89% post migration traffic growth (2019-08-29). TCGplayer (organic traffic up 95%, 2024-01-18) and Swaledale Butchers (the award) complete the list.

Two codings are judgment calls. The brand and creative code on Qodana and GitLab very likely comes from the words non brand in their titles, and the AI and PR codes on TCGplayer and Swaledale Butchers from navigation text captured as their excerpts, so the observed need is organic search, migration and commerce revenue. Cloudflare also sits on the books of transmission and semetrical.

Under KJ1 (the click replaced by the citation) it is likely, moderate confidence, that clients whose proof is traffic growth will ask for citation share next; under KJ9 (measurement worse before better) traffic proof likely weakens first.
house: Say and do: two lines tested, one practised. AI search is contradicted: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt, with 31 AI topic URLs in its sitemap; it blocks no AI crawlers. Publishing cadence is corroborated: the sitemap lists 443 URLs, 41 updated in 90 days and 147 in 365, and the newest posts on record, dated 2026-08-13 to 2026-08-27, cover content refresh, reviews and why brands that publish first win AI visibility. The deepen pass read 888 sitemap URLs and lists each recent post twice, so the sitemap likely carries duplicate entries (low confidence). The Transparency Center shows 0 Google ads and the LinkedIn check 0 ads ("0 ads match the name query"), fitting a mix with no paid media, though a LinkedIn Insight tag sits on the site. The tag stack on WordPress is GTM, LinkedIn Insight, Microsoft Clarity and iubenda, with no test tools and no ABM stack. The flagged gap is the llms.txt.
market:

openings:
The strongest opening is the AI visibility gap. SALT.agency sells AI visibility as equal to SEO and publishes the research, yet the record shows no llms.txt and no audited AI visibility product (P1 partial: no tracking, scorecard or citation share). It is likely, moderate confidence, that a rival reporting audited citation share wins the AI line at its cloud and SaaS clients, where the proof on file is traffic growth. Falsifier: a citation tracking product or scorecard from SALT.agency in a later compile, or the ESI shown as a client deliverable.

Cloudflare is the most contestable account: it also sits on the transmission and semetrical books, so it very likely buys from more than one agency. The oldest proofs, The Spectator from 2019-08-29 and Cloudflare from 2023-04-28, cannot show whether those accounts are current, a question to put to them. Exposure to KJ6 through SEO and content hours, plus no public pricing (P5 unknown), makes an outcome priced offer the sharper pitch. Displacement at 54.7 says the book does not buy mainly on price, so it is unlikely to be won on rate alone.

I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth would confirm the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.
I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the $2B milestone and pricing below $20 CPM bear on KJ2, a tailwind it reaches only through AI Search / GEO.
I1, Comscore monthly AI prompt share, Q3 report expected around December 2026: Gemini at or above 40% or ChatGPT at or below 45% would tell which assistants its citation research must track.
Its llms.txt and case library: an llms.txt, or a citation share case study after Jewson (2026-05-20), would close the strongest opening.
